# Using Gemini in Gmail and Docs to save time

By the end of this guide you’ll be able to ask Gemini to turn a tangled email chain into a short summary, write a polite reply in seconds, and tidy up a Google Doc with a single click. It’s aimed at anyone who works with Gmail and Docs every day and wants a quicker, less repetitive workflow.

## Before you start
- An eligible Google Workspace or Google AI plan. (With a personal Google account, Help me write in Gmail is currently available in the US only.)
- A computer running a modern web browser (Chrome, Edge, or Firefox) – mobile browsers also work but the steps below assume a desktop layout.
- Internet connection (Gemini runs in the cloud, so it needs to talk to Google’s servers).
- Roughly 10 minutes total: 2 minutes to open Gmail, 2 minutes to try a summary, 3 minutes to draft a reply, and 3 minutes to experiment with Docs.

## Step 1 — Summarize a long email thread in Gmail
**ACTION:** Open the email thread, then click **Ask Gemini** at the top right of Gmail.
**WHAT YOU SEE:** The Gemini side panel opens on the right, with a prompt box at the bottom.
**WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:** Type your request and click **Submit**; Gemini answers in the panel, based on the email you have open.
**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** If the side panel is closed, longer threads (more than two replies) can also show **Summarize this email** at the top of the thread — click it for a quick summary.
💬 **Example:** Type or paste the following prompt into the box:
> *"Summarize the key decisions and next-action items in this email thread for me."*
**SUCCESS CHECK:** You'll know it worked when the panel returns a short paragraph that lists the main points and any tasks assigned to you.

## Step 2 — Draft a quick email reply using Gemini
**ACTION:** In Gmail, click **Reply** to open the compose window. At the bottom, in the prompt bar, type what you want the reply to say, then click **Create**.
**WHAT YOU SEE:** A prompt bar at the bottom of the compose window. If you can't find it, click the **Help me write** icon to bring it up.
**WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:** Gemini generates a draft in the compose area, ready for you to edit.
**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** To adjust the draft, type a new instruction in the prompt bar (for example "Make it more professional") or use the **Formalize**, **Friendly** or **Shorten** buttons; the Undo and Redo icons on the right switch between drafts.
💬 **Example:** Enter a prompt such as:
> *"Write a polite email declining the Tuesday meeting because I have a scheduling conflict, and propose Thursday at 2 pm instead."*
**SUCCESS CHECK:** You'll know it worked when a fully formed paragraph appears in the compose box, containing a greeting, a brief apology, and the new meeting suggestion.

## Step 3 — Start a new Google Doc with a Gemini outline
**ACTION:** Open a blank Google Doc, click **Gemini**, and type your request in the prompt bar at the bottom. You don't need to select any text first.
**WHAT YOU SEE:** A prompt bar at the bottom of the document.
**WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:** Gemini shows its suggestions in the document. Click **Accept suggestion** for single changes, or **Accept all** / **Reject all**.
**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** If you prefer working in a panel, click **Switch to side panel** in the bottom bar after you send a prompt; **Switch to bottom bar** brings it back.
💬 **Example:** Type a prompt like:
> *"Create a professional project proposal outline for a garden-landscaping job, including sections for scope, timeline, and estimated costs."*
**SUCCESS CHECK:** You'll know it worked when the document now shows a series of headings (e.g., "Scope of Work", "Timeline", "Estimated Costs") with brief bullet points beneath each heading.

## Step 4 — Refine and polish a paragraph in Google Docs
**ACTION:** Highlight the paragraph you want to improve, then click **Refine** on the floating bar that appears.
**WHAT YOU SEE:** A list of options: **Rephrase**, **Shorten**, **More formal**, **More casual**, **Bulletize** and **Summarize** (**Elaborate** sits under **More**).
**WHAT HAPPENS NEXT:** Gemini suggests a rewritten version of the selected text; review it and click **Accept suggestion** (or **Reject all** to keep the original).
**IF IT LOOKS DIFFERENT:** You can also describe the change in your own words: click **Gemini** and mention the paragraph in your prompt.
💬 **Example:** Instead of a button, you can type a request like:
> *"Rewrite the second paragraph to sound more professional for a client newsletter."*
**SUCCESS CHECK:** You'll know it worked when the paragraph reads in a more formal tone and the new version is in the document after you accept it.

## Common mistakes
- **Sending the draft without a human check:** Gemini can draft an email, but it can also insert inaccurate dates or mis‑interpret the tone. *Fix:* Always read the draft, correct any details, and click “Send” yourself.  
- **Using a vague prompt:** A prompt like “draft an email about the project” leaves Gemini guessing the specifics. *Fix:* Include the purpose, key points, and desired tone in your prompt (e.g., “write a brief, friendly update about the project’s progress and ask for feedback”).  
- **Copy‑pasting sensitive information:** Putting client names, passwords, or confidential figures into the prompt exposes that data to the AI. *Fix:* Replace personal data with placeholders (e.g., “[Client Name]”) and only share what’s necessary for the task.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can clear a long newsletter or community‑group chain in seconds, freeing up mental space for the things you actually want to do.  
- **For your business or work:** Gemini cuts down the time you spend drafting routine replies and organizing documents, letting you focus on strategic decisions instead of repetitive typing.  
- **If you're just getting started:** The easiest first move is to try the email‑summary tool on a recent thread – no typing required, just a click and a quick read of the result.

## Try it now
Open a long email thread in Gmail, click **Ask Gemini** at the top right, and ask for a summary of the thread (or click **Summarize this email** at the top, if you see it). In under a minute you’ll see the main points appear – that’s your first win with Gemini!
